stops.name: Mamre, the covenant of the pieces
stops.campa: The word of the Lord comes to Abram in a vision: Fear not, Abram, I am thy shield, and thy exceeding great reward. He grieves that he is childless. The Lord brings him outside: Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them; so shall thy seed be. And Abram believes the Lord, and it is counted to him for righteousness. That night, between the halved carcasses, a smoking furnace and a burning lamp pass through the pieces, and God cuts the covenant, giving the land from the river of Egypt to the Euphrates.
stops.quote: Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them... So shall thy seed be. And he believed in the LORD; and he counted it to him for righteousness.

stops.name: Mamre, Hagar and the birth of Ishmael
stops.campa: Sarai, still barren, gives her Egyptian handmaid Hagar to Abram. Hagar conceives and despises her mistress; Sarai deals hardly with her, and Hagar flees into the wilderness toward Shur. By a fountain of water the angel of the Lord finds her and tells her to return, and promises: I will multiply thy seed exceedingly. She shall bear a son and call him Ishmael, for the Lord has heard her affliction. Hagar names the God who speaks to her Thou God seest me. Abram is eighty-six when Ishmael is born.
stops.quote: And she called the name of the LORD that spake unto her, Thou God seest me: for she said, Have I also here looked after him that seeth me?

stops.name: Mamre, the covenant of circumcision, the new name
stops.campa: Abram is ninety and nine when the Lord appears: I am God Almighty; walk before me, and be thou perfect. Thy name shall no more be Abram, but Abraham, for a father of many nations have I made thee. Sarai shall be Sarah, and she shall bear a son. Abraham falls on his face and laughs: shall a child be born to a man a hundred years old? God names the child Isaac. That same day Abraham circumcises himself and Ishmael and every male of his house, the sign of the everlasting covenant cut into the flesh.
stops.quote: Neither shall thy name any more be called Abram, but thy name shall be Abraham; for a father of many nations have I made thee.

stops.name: Mamre, the Three Visitors at the tent door
stops.campa: The Lord appears to Abraham by the oaks of Mamre as he sits in the tent door in the heat of the day. He lifts his eyes and behold, three men stand by him. He runs to meet them, bows to the earth, and hastens a feast: a calf tender and good, cakes of fine meal, butter and milk; and stands by them under the tree while they eat. Where is Sarah thy wife? one asks. I will certainly return, and Sarah shall have a son. Behind the tent flap Sarah laughs within herself. Is any thing too hard for the Lord?
stops.quote: And he said, I will certainly return unto thee according to the time of life; and, lo, Sarah thy wife shall have a son. And Sarah heard it in the tent door, which was behind him.

stops.name: The heights above Sodom, the intercession
stops.campa: The men turn toward Sodom, and the Lord says: Shall I hide from Abraham that thing which I do? The cry of Sodom is great; He will go down and see. Abraham draws near and pleads: Wilt thou also destroy the righteous with the wicked? Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right? For fifty righteous, the city is spared; for forty-five; for forty; thirty; twenty; and at last for ten. Each time the Lord consents. But ten are not found. Abraham stands in the place where he stood before the Lord, and watches.
stops.quote: That be far from thee to do after this manner, to slay the righteous with the wicked... Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?

stops.name: Sodom, the rescue of Lot and the pillar of salt
stops.campa: At evening the two angels come to Sodom, where Lot sits in the gate. He takes them in; the men of the city besiege the house. The angels strike them blind and seize Lot's hand: Escape for thy life; look not behind thee. Then the Lord rains upon Sodom and Gomorrah brimstone and fire out of heaven, and overthrows the cities and all the plain. Lot's wife looks back, and she becomes a pillar of salt. Abraham rises early and looks toward the plain: the smoke of the country goes up as the smoke of a furnace.
stops.quote: But his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.

stops.name: Gerar: Sarah and Abimelech, the sojourn in the south
stops.campa: Abraham journeys south and sojourns in Gerar, and again says of Sarah, She is my sister. Abimelech the king sends and takes her. But God comes to Abimelech in a dream by night: Behold, thou art but a dead man, for the woman is a man's wife. Abimelech, who has not touched her, protests his innocence; God bids him restore her, for Abraham is a prophet and shall pray for him. At dawn Abimelech gives Sarah back with sheep and oxen and silver, and Abraham prays, and the wombs of Abimelech's house are healed.
stops.quote: Now therefore restore the man his wife; for he is a prophet, and he shall pray for thee, and thou shalt live.

stops.name: The birth of Isaac, laughter in the tent
stops.campa: The Lord visits Sarah as He has said, and does unto her as He has spoken. Sarah conceives and bears Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of which God had spoken. Abraham is a hundred years old. He names him Isaac, laughter, and circumcises him on the eighth day. And Sarah says: God hath made me to laugh, so that all that hear will laugh with me. The child of the impossible promise, the son of the free woman, is at the breast; and Abraham makes a great feast the day Isaac is weaned.
stops.quote: And Sarah said, God hath made me to laugh, so that all that hear will laugh with me.

stops.name: Beersheba, the casting out of Hagar, the well and the boy
stops.campa: Sarah sees Ishmael mocking and demands the bondwoman and her son be cast out. The thing is grievous to Abraham, but God tells him to hearken, for in Isaac shall his seed be called; yet of Ishmael too He will make a nation. Abraham rises early, gives Hagar bread and a bottle of water, and sends her away; she wanders in the wilderness of Beersheba. The water spent, she lays the child under a shrub and weeps apart, not to see him die. But God hears the boy, and the angel calls: Fear not. God opens her eyes: a well of water.
stops.quote: Fear not; for God hath heard the voice of the lad where he is.

stops.name: Beersheba, the oath and the tamarisk
stops.campa: Abimelech and Phichol his captain come to Abraham: God is with thee in all that thou doest; swear that thou wilt not deal falsely. Abraham reproves them over a well of water his servants' men had seized, and sets seven ewe lambs apart as witness that he digged the well. So they swear, and the place is called Beersheba, the well of the oath, the well of seven. There Abraham plants a tamarisk tree and calls on the name of the Lord, the everlasting God, and sojourns in the land of the Philistines many days.
stops.quote: And Abraham planted a grove in Beersheba, and called there on the name of the LORD, the everlasting God.

stops.name: Mecca, Hagar and Ishmael in the barren valley
stops.campa: In the Islamic canon Ibrahim brings Hajar and the infant Isma'il to a valley without cultivation by God's sacred House, and leaves them there with a skin of water and dates, trusting the command. When the water is gone and the child cries with thirst, Hajar runs in her distress between the two hills of Safa and Marwah, seven times, searching. At the child's heel the ground breaks open and water gushes up. She dams it, crying Zamzam (stop!), and the well of Zamzam flows to this day, the water that will never fail.
stops.quote: O my Lord! I have made some of my offspring to dwell in a valley without cultivation, by Thy Sacred House.

stops.name: Mecca, raising the foundations of the Kaaba
stops.campa: Ibrahim returns to his grown son Isma'il, and together they raise the foundations of the House at Bakkah, the first House appointed for mankind, laying stone on stone in the naked valley. Ibrahim stands on a rock to reach the rising wall, and the stone softens under his feet and keeps the print of them, the Maqam Ibrahim, the Station of Abraham, that stands beside the Kaaba still. As they build, father and son pray that God accept the work and make of their seed a people submitting to Him.
stops.quote: And remember when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House with Ishmael, praying, Our Lord! Accept this from us. Indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
